procedure.description: suction assisted lipectomy, trunk and lower extremities, for lipedema

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Lanternhill Health Plan denied the claim for CPT 15877 (suction assisted lipectomy, trunk and lower extremities, for lipedema) with date of service 2026-06-23. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Documentation does not establish failure of conservative therapy.

criteria.text: Diagnosis of lipedema stage II or III documented on examination: bilateral symmetric disproportionate adiposity of the limbs sparing the feet, negative Stemmer sign, tenderness, and easy bruising.
At least 6 months of conservative therapy including compression garments and manual lymphatic drainage or supervised exercise, with persistent pain or functional impairment.
Pain or impaired mobility attributable to lipedema.

chart.text: Thyroid labs back. TSH 3.3, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 75. Repeat in a year.
From the referring physician: please evaluate for surgical management. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 20. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.

39 year old woman here about her legs, self-referred after reading about lipedema. Mother and aunt had the same legs. Discussed lymph-sparing liposuction, staged, and that it is debulking, not a cure. Her history otherwise: prediabetes, diet controlled, anxiety, sees a counselor. Surgeries: a C-section. Allergies: codeine makes her sick. Never smoked, occasional beer, has three kids at home. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Classic picture. Column legs out of all proportion to her waist, cuff sign at the ankles, feet spared, Stemmer negative, exquisitely tender to pinch over the thighs, bruises if you look at her. Stage 3. Says she cannot stand through a shift anymore, pain in the thighs is constant, stairs are hard because the legs knock together.
Patient called about a tick bite on the scalp after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.
Vitamin D came back 23. Started 2000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 13 and 17. No ocular pathology noted.

Knee pain going down stairs, left side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.
Blood pressure check. 127 over 88 today, 138 over 85 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 40 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 6 weeks.
Follow-up. Reviewed photos and measurements, legs unchanged. Went over the staged plan and the compression afterward. Vitals today 122 over 86, pulse 70.
Message from the patient about scheduling. Wants a date in the next couple of months if the insurance comes through. Passed to the surgery scheduler.
Mammogram report forwarded for the record. Bilateral screening, BI-RADS 1, negative, routine screening in one year.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.
Check-in while we wait on the insurance. No change in the complaints. Reviewed the risks and recovery one more time, she remains sure about going ahead.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.

Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 190, LDL 141, HDL 48, triglycerides 143. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
Work note requested for a sick day last Thursday. Faxed to the employer.

Twisted the left ankle stepping off a curb 4 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.

Here with a cough and congestion for 8 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
A1c came back 6.1. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.
Pre-op for stage one, thighs. Consent signed. Marked standing. Garments ordered.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, she will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.

expected.note: The chart never addresses crit-2 (conservative); no entry supports it, so an appeal would assert what the record does not contain.
